title: Monotherapy with major antihypertensive drug classes and risk of hospital admissions for mood disorders
authors: Boal AH, Smith DJ, McCallum L, Muir S, Touyz RM, Dominiczak AF, et al.
population: Patients aged 40 to 80 years with antihypertensive exposure over 90 days in a Glasgow hospital database of 525,046 patients, analysed by monotherapy class
funder: S. Padmanabhan is funded by the Medical Research Council (MR/M016560/1 and The AIM-HY Study) and the British Heart Foundation (PG/12/85/29925 and CS/16/1/31878); D.J. Smith by a Lister Institute Prize Fellowship; L. McCallum by a BHF fellowship (FS/14/52/30901); A.F. Dominiczak has funding from the Scottish Ecosystem for Precision Medicine.
result: 299 hospital admissions with a mood disorder, median time 847 days. Against ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers, which had the lowest risk, calcium antagonists had a hazard ratio of 2.28 (95% CI 1.13 to 4.58) and beta blockers 2.11 (1.12 to 3.98); no antihypertensive 1.63 (0.94 to 2.82) and thiazides 1.56 (0.65 to 3.73). The authors describe the findings as exploratory.
